images.note: Beat: Bessemer's steel-making process (patented 1856) makes cheap steel possible. Primary is a contemporary c.1895 photograph of workers with a Bessemer converter at the Pennsylvania Steel Company's plant, Steelton PA (Hagley, Accession 1980.300), 3701x4652. Alt is a different object: a 1:3 scale model of a Bessemer converter, c.1865 (SMG object 1984-652), 1380x1536.
images.title: Workers with a Bessemer converter, Pennsylvania Steel Co., Steelton PA, c.1895

images.note: Beat: hard (anthracite) coal lets factories ditch water power. Two DIFFERENT Lewis Hine 1911 anthracite photographs from different institutions. Primary: 'Coalbreakers, Pittston, Pennsylvania,' January 1911 (MoMA 21.1992), 2000x1380. Alt: 'Breaker Boys In Coal Chute, South Pittston, Pennsylvania,' 1911 (AIC), 2000x1458. AIC's IIIF omits Content-Length on HEAD; ranged GET confirmed ~671KB JPEG. Both 1911, documenting the same anthracite industry the script's coal beat describes.
images.source: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), New York
images.title: Lewis Hine, Coalbreakers, Pittston PA, January 1911

images.note: Beat: Rockefeller consolidates oil refining (horizontal integration, the trust). Primary is a period ambrotype portrait of a young John D. Rockefeller by William C. North, c.1860s (CMA 2023.130), 2913x3400 -- closest in time to the 1870s-80s trust era. Alt is a different likeness: Timothy Cole's 1921 wood engraving after John Singer Sargent (Buffalo AKG 1940:13, public domain, gift of John D. Rockefeller Jr.), 1975x2500 -- later but the iconic Rockefeller image.
images.title: William C. North, ambrotype portrait of John D. Rockefeller, c.1860s
